_doc: Which OpenClaw agents may run shell commands, and until when. Enforced by scripts/check-agent-exec-policy.py
(PR Validation, and post-deploy with --live on node-8). The RULES live in that script as constants; this file only
records each agent's posture, so a PR cannot widen a rule by editing data.
posture=denied: the agent's tools.deny carries every shell-capable tool for its profile (the script's REQUIRED_DENY:
exec + process + lobster + nodes + computer + terminal on main; exec on edge). exec also removes the codex aliases
gateway_exec / node_exec / sandbox_exec, and - because exec is outside the codex harness's audited safe-deny set -
the codex-native shell. Cost, accepted per agent: the restricted harness also drops native web_search, skill_search,
memories, browser_use and every MCP server (scripts/validate-config-matrix.sh check #8, incident 2026-09-10).
posture=full: the agent keeps exec (security=full, ask=off, root on node-8). Allowed ONLY with a reason, a ruling
reference, an exit plan and an expiry no more than 31 days out; CI goes red the day after expiry. A non-ops agent
that is denied on main can never come back to full, and a new agent can never start at full (--base check).
Why not tools.exec.security deny/allowlist per agent: on openclaw 2026.8.35 every main agent runs the codex harness
and @openclaw/codex refuses a turn whose effective exec mode is deny/allowlist (AgentHarnessPreflightError), so the
fallback runner silently moves the agent to openrouter on the embedded runtime. The script rejects that shape.
Why not reason/expiry inside openclaw-main.json: its schema is additionalProperties:false at every level, so an
unknown key stops the gateway from starting.

scout.note: Reads the open web (373 web_fetch + ~3,300 native searches in 14d) = the most injectable main agent; 150 shell calls in 14d (muso-read.sh SQL ~55, the rest reading skill files). Accepted cost: the restricted codex harness turns native web_search/web_run OFF (verified in @openclaw/codex resolveCodexWebSearchPlan: restricted -> kind=managed, hydra configures no managed provider). Canary after deploy: scripts/redteam/exec_injection_probe.py --agent scout and --check-search. Revert = remove scout's deny entries (and its HARNESS_DENY_EXCEPTIONS rows) in one PR.

finance.reason: Was full for Stripe reporting (339 stripe CLI calls in 14d, 312 via gateway_exec for Secret Store env) until its dated exception expired on 2026-11-08. An expired posture resolves to DENIED, never to 'carry on': the deploy was blocked on 2026-11-09 and that block was correct behaviour.
finance.exit: The route back is the exit plan that was already written: one read-only wrapper stripe-report.sh run by a cron that posts its output to finance's channel, so finance consumes text and never runs it. Renaming the posture back to full is NOT a data edit - see the note below.
finance.note: Fail-safe applied under firstmate ruling [key=exec-posture-lapsed] 2026-11-09: deny now, hold the capability question for the captain. A renewal is deliberately NOT reachable by editing this file: check-agent-exec-policy.py's base rule rejects a RE-GRANT to a non-ops agent, so the captain's decision lands as a reviewed change to that script's rules. Cost accepted meanwhile: no Stripe reporting, and (because exec is outside the codex safe-deny set) no native web_search / skill_search / memories / MCP either.

qa.reason: Was full for the review pipeline (26,132 calls in 14d: qa-gh.sh, qa-review-clone.sh, qa-review-status.sh, qa-pr-approve.sh, qa-slack-dm.sh) until its dated exception expired on 2026-11-08. RESIDUAL RISK, now closed rather than renewed: qa reads attacker-authored PR text, so an expired exec=full posture on that agent is the worst of the two failures.
qa.exit: The route back is the exit plan that was already written: PR bodies/diffs reach qa as fenced data, every qa-*.sh refuses argv/stdin without the dispatch nonce, then T9 moves qa to its own gateway (pods/qa-review-gateway). Renaming the posture back to full is NOT a data edit - see the note below.
qa.note: Fail-safe applied under firstmate ruling [key=exec-posture-lapsed] 2026-11-09: deny now, hold the capability question for the captain. A renewal is deliberately NOT reachable by editing this file: check-agent-exec-policy.py's base rule rejects a RE-GRANT to a non-ops agent, so the captain's decision lands as a reviewed change to that script's rules. Cost accepted meanwhile: qa reviews nothing, and (because exec is outside the codex safe-deny set) it also loses native web_search / skill_search / memories / MCP.

cto.reason: Engineering shell (5,650 bash + 1,254 gateway_exec in 14d: gh, git, kubectl, muso-read.sh). Reads PR bodies and GitHub = untrusted, second-highest risk.
cto.exit: Every untrusted read goes through a no-exec reader agent whose output comes back as quoted data; then an allowlist or deny.

ceo.reason: 966 bash + 333 gateway_exec in 14d (muso CLI, gh, muso-admin-api, skill reads).
ceo.exit: Untrusted reads through the no-exec reader agent; then an allowlist or deny.

cmo.exit: Untrusted reads through the no-exec reader agent; then an allowlist or deny.

operations.reason: Ops agent: acts only for god-mode requesters; its exec runs the ops wrappers (muso CLI, intercom-ops-write.sh, agent-bridge-request.sh, muso-admin-api.sh, stripe). Already on the restricted harness (web_fetch/web_search deny).
operations.exit: Allowlist of its named wrapper scripts.

devops.reason: Ops agent: kubectl, journalctl, systemctl, prod-log fetchers; acts only for god-mode requesters.
devops.exit: Allowlist of its named wrapper scripts.

clio.reason: Ops/coordination agent: rg, gh, kubectl, muso CLI; acts only for god-mode requesters.
clio.exit: Allowlist of its named wrapper scripts.
